title: ui tests: stop pinning the exact ObjectSchema key count in app-shell corpus guards, since every additive spec key turns Test UI red for all ui PRs
body:
Filed by seat `domain:ui#1` (seat post #25966) · `os-steve` · session `session_017iXjUm1rujwDk7f3KT1Pkk`, at the maintainer's request in the project for a structural fix after #26218. ⛔ Not a claim.

## What was measured

- `ui/packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.retiredObjectEnabled.test.ts:161` and `MetadataService.specKeyObjectPayload.test.ts:175` each assert `expect(Object.keys(ObjectSchema.shape).length).toBe(N)` ("corpus guard"). The comments above the first one record six re-points: 42→43 (`editMode`), 44 (`imageField`), 45 (`attachedOnRead`), 46 (`defaultRowScope`), 47 (`membershipKeys`), and now 48 (`sharing`, #26005 → #26218 / #26231).
- Each time, an **additive** spec key that these files do not read turned `Test UI` red on every ui PR's merge ref. #26005 merged on 2026-10-26 with Test UI skipped by its path filter (closing that gap is #26092), and the ui merge queue then stalled until #26231.
- The comment itself says that the spec-adoption fact belongs to `packages/types/src/__tests__/object-schema-metadata-spec-derivation.test.ts`, and that the count only rides along as a guard for the membership assertions below it (`enable` present, `enabled` / `_deleted` / soft-delete aliases absent).

## Ask

Make these guards independent of how many keys `ObjectSchema` has. Measure first which of these holds, then do one:

- Assert only the membership claims the files are about, and drop the exact count. The types-package derivation test already pins adoption.
- Or derive the expected set from the spec's own `authorable-surface/data.json` instead of a literal.

⛔ Do not weaken any membership assertion. Also sweep `ui/` for other exact-count pins on spec-owned shapes (e.g. `Object.keys(<Spec>Schema.shape)` with `toBe(<n>)` or `toHaveLength(<n>)`), list them in the PR, and convert those of the same kind.

## Business reason

Who benefits: every ui PR. An additive change in another lane, which by definition breaks no ui behaviour, should not stop the ui merge queue. Today it costs a p1 card and a full queue round for both ui seats each time.

## Who acts on it

The `domain:ui` seat that owns app-shell services (seat 1). Test-only and app-shell, so no sdui record moves. It lands after #26231, which edits the same two files.

## Duplicate check

`search_issues` on objectstack-ai/objectstack, open, "ObjectSchema shape count pin accept.size ui test": only #26218, the one-time re-point. #26092 covers the CI filter half, not this test design.
